tagline: One lane, no center line, and a pass nobody plows.
intro: East of Arnold, Highway 4 climbs past the Bear Valley turnoff and along the north side of Lake Alpine. Past the Mount Reba road it narrows. From there it is one lane with no center line, steep and full of tight switchbacks, over Pacific Grade Summit at 8,050 feet and Ebbetts Pass at 8,730, then down to Markleeville and Route 89.

Merchants in Murphys had the road built to carry supplies to the silver miners east of the Sierra, and it became a toll road in 1862. The pass is named for John Ebbetts, who hoped to put a railroad over it. He surveyed near it and found it would not do.

moments.title: Arnold
moments.text: The town is named for Bob and Bernice Arnold, who opened the Ebbetts Pass Inn here in 1927 for travelers on the pass road and visitors to the big trees nearby.

moments.title: Lake Alpine
moments.text: A reservoir on Silver Creek at 7,303 feet, with the highway passing along its north side on the way up to Pacific Grade Summit.

moments.title: Ebbetts Pass
moments.text: The Pacific Crest Trail crosses the highway at the top. On the way down the east side many hairpins are blind and steepen at the apex, and most cars want first gear.

practical: Not suitable for large trucks, buses, RVs or long trailers. Ebbetts Pass is not plowed and usually closes from November until as late as May.
